issues.title: [Bug]: foreach accepts an iterable object whose completion type includes error
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: the program compiles and then panics at run time. Spec §7.22.1 requires the foreach iterable's iteration completion type to be nil. Here it is error?, so the foreach line must be a compile-time error. A clean-context spec check agreed (high confidence). The type checker is missing the check and no crash occurs, so this is frontend and not frontend-crash. No duplicate found. #1302 is the opposite case.

issues.title: [Bug]: xml:slice requires endIndex although it is defaultable
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: missing required parameter 'endIndex'
 --> i1401.bal:5:16
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: missing required parameter 'endIndex'
 --> i1401.bal:6:16
ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. lang.xml declares slice(xml x, int startIndex, int endIndex = x.length()), so slice(1) and xml:slice(x, 2) must compile and print <b/><c/> and <c/>. A clean-context spec check agreed (high confidence). This is a lang library declaration issue: the opaque registry entry is missing the default. No duplicate found. #910, which covered opaque defaults, is closed.

issues.title: [Bug]: float:toBitsInt returns different results for the single NaN value
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec §5.2.4.1 says all IEEE NaN bit patterns are a single Ballerina value, and === agrees (it prints true). toBitsInt is a function of that value, so it must return one int for every NaN. A clean-context spec check agreed (medium-high confidence: the spec does not name which canonical bit pattern to use). This is lang.float. No duplicate found. #391 and #394 are about NaN equality.

issues.title: [Bug]: decimal % panics when the integer quotient exceeds 34 digits
issues.output:
error: not a valid decimal
        at main(i1403.bal:5)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: the program panics at run time. The spec defines decimal % as the exact x - y*n rounded once, with no exceptions for finite operands. 10^35 mod 7 = 5 and 10^40 mod 3 = 1 are both exact. A clean-context spec check agreed (high confidence). The remainder operator fails in the runtime, so this is backend. No duplicate found. #1347 (decimal division exponent) is a different bug.

issues.title: [Bug]: return-type annotations are not encoded in BIR or exposed to native code
issues.output:
1
(program runs; bir.BIRFunction (bir/model.go:119) has no return-annotation field, and extern.FunctionMetadata (runtime/extern/handle.go:58) exposes only Params/RestParam)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main by code inspection. The AST has ReturnAnnotationAttachments, but BIRFunction has no field for them and extern.FunctionMetadata does not expose them, so native code cannot read the return annotation. Runtime-visible annotations must survive into the compiled form, which makes this valid. BIR generation drops the data and there is no crash, so this is frontend. It is already a sub-issue of #1355, and #1361 is the sibling issue for method annotations. I did not run a clean-context subagent because the reproducer's printed output cannot show the defect; validity was judged from the code.

notes: Reproduced against upstream main @72d94f9b. #1304, #1303 and #1282 were skipped: they were already reported (2026-10-20, as undetermined) and have not been updated since.
